key_insight: MedPrune makes medical VQA multi-agent collaboration more efficient by dynamically pruning irrelevant specialist nodes and low-value communication edges while preserving diagnostic reasoning quality.
engineering_relevance: The paper is relevant to AI-enabled engineering systems because it shows how topology optimization can reduce communication overhead and improve token-efficient coordination in heterogeneous agent networks.
method: Formulate the diagnostic workflow as a heterogeneous communication graph with specialist agents as nodes and intra-/inter-department links as edges.
Use reinforcement learning to perform heterogeneous node sparsification and remove task-irrelevant agents.
Apply heterogeneous edge sparsification to keep only diagnostically salient connections while balancing performance and topology complexity.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on medical VQA in both full-set and few-shot settings, where it outperforms multi-agent baselines and improves token efficiency with reported adversarial robustness.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the learned pruning policy, so unstable topology decisions could affect generalization or deployment reliability.
paper_title: MedPrune: Topology-Efficient Multimodal Multi-Agent Communication Evolution for Medical VQA Tasks
